errors.text: The proposed intervention is an unspecified substitution of Hf and Ta with Ti and Nb rather than the specific addition of 4.2 at.% Cr.
No substitution fraction or unique alloy composition is given, so the intervention is not a single reproducible treatment.
The hypothesis omits the approximately 4 vol.% reticulated Cr2(Ti,Zr,Hf,Ta) Laves phase that mediates the target strength-ductility improvement.
The proposed generic solution-strengthening mechanism does not account for crack deflection or plasticity compensation by the interconnected Laves-phase network.
Temperature, strain rate, specimen geometry, and loading mode are not specified adequately, despite the request for explicit boundary conditions.
The falsification rule is not quantitative; terms such as 'significantly reduced' provide no predetermined rejection threshold.

The cited lower-density HfNbTaTiZr result directly shows severe high-temperature strength loss, so it does not support the claim that light-element substitution will preserve elevated-temperature performance.
